title: Pad See Ew
subtitle: Thai stir-fried wide rice noodles with egg and broccoli
excerpt: The great Thai stir-fried noodle: wide flat rice noodles cooked over very high heat until lightly charred and smoky, with egg, Chinese broccoli, and chicken in a sweet-salty dark soy sauce. Simpler than Pad Thai and often preferred for its direct, caramelised flavour.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pad see ew (stir-fried soy sauce) is one of Thailand's most popular street noodle dishes and a common lunch in both Thailand and Thai restaurants worldwide. It uses wide flat rice noodles (sen yai), which become silky and slightly chewy when stir-fried; fresh noodles are preferable to dried for this dish. The defining technique is obtaining the wok hei (breath of the wok): the caramelisation and slight charring of the noodles from very high heat that gives the dish its characteristic smoky sweetness. This is difficult to achieve on a domestic hob, which cannot reach the temperatures of a commercial wok burner; the workaround is to use a very small amount of oil, cook in batches, and let the noodles sit untouched for 30 to 40 seconds so they can develop colour before tossing.

recipeTools.notes: The largest, heaviest frying pan or wok you own.

content.text: The biggest mistake is crowding the pan: stir-fry in batches if needed. Let the noodles sit in contact with the hot pan for 30 to 40 seconds to develop char rather than constantly tossing them. Fresh wide rice noodles (from Asian supermarkets) give the best result; if using dried, soak them in cold water for 30 minutes until pliable but not soft.

items.preparation: wide flat rice noodles; fresh if possible, or dried soaked in cold water for 30 minutes
or Chinese broccoli (gai lan); stems halved, leaves roughly chopped

content.text: Mix the sauce: combine the dark soy, light soy, oyster sauce, sugar, and rice vinegar. Heat a large, heavy pan or wok over the highest possible heat until smoking. Add 2 tablespoons of oil and stir-fry the chicken in a single layer for 2 to 3 minutes until cooked and lightly charred. Remove from the pan.

Add the remaining oil to the same pan. Add the garlic and fry for 20 seconds. Add the noodles and spread them in a single layer. Let them sit for 30 to 40 seconds until they start to char, then toss. Push to the side, add the beaten eggs, and scramble briefly. Add the pak choi stems and stir-fry for 1 minute.

Return the chicken and add the pak choi leaves. Pour the sauce over everything and toss vigorously for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is coated and the noodles are darkened and slightly charred in places. Serve immediately.
